assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and realised with strontium by both groups, brought atomic clocks to the 10^-18 level. That is a clear, original and lasting advance in precision atomic physics. It underpins tests of fundamental constants and relativity, relativistic geodesy and the prospective redefinition of the second. From my vantage in atomic theory, the control of systematic shifts such as blackbody radiation, lattice light shifts and collisions is exceptional experimental physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early strontium lattice clocks. Ye's JILA group drove the record stability and accuracy and the many-body clock work. The supplied credit has exactly these two names, which gives a clean, defensible two-person configuration. Other groups (for example at PTB, NIST, SYRTE) contributed, but I do not see a competing decisive claim.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many laboratories worldwide across Sr, Yb and Hg. Performance has improved steadily and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely; a later redefinition of the SI second would add weight, but the discovery stands without it.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would see this as too close to the 2005 and 2012 recognition of frequency combs and trapped-ion control.
My recollection of the exact attribution between the Katori and Ye groups for the first lattice clocks is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices turned the Bose-Hubbard and Fermi-Hubbard models into laboratory systems. The Mott-insulator transition, single-site quantum gas microscopy and entanglement and thermalisation studies followed. The conceptual originality, in the proposal that cold atoms can realise strongly correlated Hamiltonians, is high. The impact on many-body physics is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: The theory proposal for the superfluid to Mott transition came from the Innsbruck group (Zoller, with Jaksch and others, and Cirac in related quantum-simulation work). The experimental realisation was by Greiner, Bloch and Hänsch, and Esslinger's group achieved the fermionic regime. Five names are credited, so a three-person prize forces hard choices. A theorist plus the two experimentalists of the first Mott observation is one coherent option, but Cirac, Esslinger and Jaksch are all arguably decisive.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and extended by many groups. The field is mature, with quantum gas microscopes and analogue simulators in wide use. Timing is reasonable, although the 2001 BEC prize and the 2012 prize for quantum-optical control of single systems partly overlap in subject area.
uncertainties: Unresolved allocation among five credited people, with Cirac, Esslinger and Jaksch plausible alternatives.
Whether analogue quantum simulation has yet produced a result that solves a problem beyond classical computation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BB84 protocol and Ekert's entanglement-based E91 protocol founded quantum cryptography. They showed that quantum measurement limits can be turned into information-theoretic security. The originality is high and the conceptual impact on quantum information is lasting. It has also spawned a deployed technology, with satellite links and fibre networks.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced BB84 in 1984. Ekert independently proposed an entanglement and Bell-inequality based protocol in 1991. The supplied credited names list Ekert in two spelling variants, which I treat as one person and use the 'Artur K. Ekert' string. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a known historical precursor but is not among the credited names. A three-person prize is feasible with these names.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations are numerous, from early free-space links to satellite-based QKD, and entanglement-based tests relate to the 2022 Bell-test prize. Practical security is still debated because of device imperfections and side channels. The foundational idea is stable, so timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as more information science than physics.
The precursor claim of Stephen Wiesner is not represented in the credited names.
Practical-security loopholes do not undermine the principle, but they bear on how mature the technology is.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles in bilayer graphene and their experimental realisation opened a new field of strongly correlated moiré quantum matter, with correlated insulators, superconductivity and fractional Chern states. It is a rare case of a quantitative theoretical prediction followed rapidly by striking experiments. The impact on condensed matter physics has been very large and is still growing.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 continuum-model prediction of flat bands near 1.1 degrees. Jarillo-Herrero's group experimentally observed the correlated insulator and superconductivity in 2018. The credited names fit a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration. Others, such as Dean, Young, Yacoby and Efetov, also contributed experimentally, but they are not credited in the supplied entry.
assessment.maturity: Replicated independently by many groups, and the platform has expanded to twisted TMDs and related systems. Core observations are firm. Some of the physics, such as the pairing mechanism and the origin of some topological states, is still developing, so recognition could be premature by some years.
uncertainties: The superconductivity mechanism in magic-angle graphene is not settled.
Allocation among experimentalists not credited here.
Possible prematurity relative to the stability of the interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recollision (three-step) model explains high-harmonic generation and strong-field ionisation through tunnelling, acceleration and recombination, and it is the conceptual basis for attosecond pulse generation and attosecond metrology. The originality, clarity and lasting influence are exceptional. I note that attosecond science was recognised by the 2023 prize, so the question is whether the foundational model deserves separate recognition.
assessment.attribution: Corkum's 1993 paper gave the classical recollision picture, and Schafer and collaborators, including Kulander, proposed it in the same year. Lewenstein and colleagues, with L'Huillier, supplied the quantum-mechanical strong-field approximation in 1994. The supplied credit omits Kulander, who is a significant contributor to the Schafer et al. work, and I cannot add him. I should disclose that I have worked with Anne L'Huillier and the Lund attosecond community. I have no documented collaboration with the three credited names.
assessment.maturity: Very well confirmed experimentally and theoretically for three decades. The interpretation is stable. Because the 2023 prize addressed the experimental generation and the foundational discoveries of attosecond pulses, a further prize in the same area may be seen as less timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 physics prize and whether the committee would return to the area.
Kulander's absence from the credited names affects the fairness of the configuration.
My professional proximity to the field could bias my view in either direction.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapping and cooling antiprotons and antihydrogen, and then spectroscopy and gravity tests with them, enabled direct comparisons of matter and antimatter, including 1S-2S spectroscopy, hyperfine structure and charge neutrality. It is high-precision atomic physics aimed at CPT and the baryon asymmetry. The experimental achievement is remarkable, but the discovery so far is the capability and tight null tests, not a violation of any symmetry.
assessment.attribution: Gabrielse led the ATRAP effort, with a long record on single-particle traps and the electron and proton magnetic moments, and Hangst leads ALPHA, which demonstrated the first antihydrogen trapping and spectroscopy. Other antihydrogen creators (ATHENA, Amoretti, Fujiwara) and the earlier CERN-LEAR work on antiprotons are not credited. The two supplied names make a plausible but contestable pairing.
assessment.maturity: Results are reproducible within and across collaborations, with steady precision improvements. The interpretation is stable, but because no deviation from the Standard Model has been found, the case rests on technical achievement, which makes recognition somewhat early.
uncertainties: Competing claims from ATHENA, ATRAP and ALPHA for first antihydrogen and trapping.
Significance depends on future precision or a deviation from CPT.
Whether ATRAP and ALPHA credit should both be recognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of a Higgs-like boson at the LHC confirmed the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking and completed the Standard Model's particle content. Its significance is among the highest in recent physics. The 2013 prize recognised the theoretical prediction, so the experimental discovery has no prize of its own; I treat it as an open question of fair recognition rather than a new discovery.
assessment.attribution: The discovery came from two large collaborations of thousands of people. The credited names, Gianotti, Jenni, Della Negra and Virdee, are leaders and spokespersons or founders, not the sole decisive contributors. I choose three of the four and cannot say that Virdee's contribution is less than the others'. The prize rules prevent honouring the collaborations and make any individual choice somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Very strongly confirmed, with combined ATLAS and CMS measurements and ongoing coupling studies. Mature and timely if the committee decides that an experimental prize is possible.
uncertainties: No fair attribution to individuals exists within the three-person limit.
Virdee's omission is as defensible as any other selection among the four.
The committee may consider the 2013 prize to have addressed this discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 classification of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators, together with their experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells, created a field of topological quantum matter with a wide influence on condensed matter physics. The theoretical idea is original and elegant, and the experimental verification was direct.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 topological insulator in graphene (2005). Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the effect in HgTe, and Molenkamp's group observed it in 2007. The credited names omit Zhang and Bernevig, who made the key HgTe prediction, so the supplied credit leaves a gap in the experimental-theory chain. The 2016 prize for topological phase transitions in matter partly overlaps in subject.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across many materials, including 3D topological insulators and later quantum anomalous Hall systems. The interpretation is stable. Practical applications remain elusive, which does not undermine the fundamental importance.
uncertainties: Missing credit to Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang for the HgTe proposal.
Overlap with the 2016 prize for topological matter.
Whether the quantum spin Hall experiment is the decisive element or the Z2 theory is.
